newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Thousands homeless in floods in southern Africa.
newsitem.headline: Thousands homeless in floods in southern Africa.

text.p: Tens of thousands of people have been left homeless by flooding in three southern African countries, officials said on Monday.
In Malawi and Mozambique, which share the same rivers as they run east towards the Indian Ocean, food and blankets have been airdropped to villages isolated by floods.

In Zimbabwe, seven weeks of non-stop rain have swept dams away and destroyed crops and villages, mostly in the east and north-east. The rains have flooded many untarred roads but officials said the situation was manageable.
Malawi President Bakili Muluzi declared the southern districts of Chikwawa and Nsanje disaster areas after flying over the extensive region on Sunday.

Luke Banda, Malawi's coordinator for the Ministry of Relief and Rehabilitation, told Reuters at least 80,000 people, 20,000 of them families from neighbouring Mozambique who crossed the river frontier, had been displaced by flooding on the Shire and Luo rivers.
Rain has fallen on Malawi all month. Banda said there had been unconfirmed reports several people trying to cross the Shire river had drowned.
"There are also fears there are casualties that we don't know about. Some people were seen clinging to trees waiting for help and we don't know what has happened to them," he said.
The Malawi government has begun to airlift maize, beans and blankets to victims of what one official said was the country's worst flooding since 1947.
The Shire joins the Zambezi river in Mozambique where thousands of people have also been left homeless in central provinces. The South African Air Force has helped airdrop aid.
The Mozambican government on Monday described the situation, particularly in the Zambezi river valley, as "very critical".
The cabinet is due to meet later this week to consider if to declare the two provinces of Manhica and Sofala disaster areas.
The worst floods were reported on the Pungue river, but authorities said water levels had started to decrease on the river which enters Mozambique from Zimbabwe.
Monday's Noticias newspaper said 15 students whose canoe capsized on the Zambezi on Friday from Maputo were missing.
